audit_findings.magnitude: $227.0m FY2026 digital-asset gain and $216.1m year-end digital assets; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The gain could inflate FY2026 OE and its log-trend anchor, while the related assets could also enter the stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Other non-operating income, net for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 was $245.2 million, compared to Other non-operating expenses, net of $7.1 million for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, primarily as a result of non-cash Gains on Digital Assets of $227.0 million in the current year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large non-cash gain and shows a $231.4m cash-flow reversal, but the supplied OE calculation does not establish whether that reversal carried through to OE or whether digital assets and CNTN interests are included in stakes_net. No valuation error is yet demonstrated, but $227.0m is 22.7% of the $1,001.1m anchor and is reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile net earnings to FY2026 OE line by line; identify the treatment of the $227.0m gain, $16.5m coin revenue, $216.1m digital assets, $31.6m warrants and CNTN shares; then rerun the anchor and scenarios if any duplication or retained gain is found.

audit_findings.title: The four-year anchor may rest on an erroneous amortization rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $196.6m FY2025 acquired-intangible amortization mismatch; anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A classification or double-counting error could invalidate excluded historical OE observations and change the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization of intangible assets that relate to past acquisitions will recur in future periods until such intangible assets have been fully amortized.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that the cited FY2025 excess exactly equals separately filed acquired-intangible amortization of $196.6m, but it does not establish whether the rail omitted that component or counted it twice. Because six years were discarded and the $1,001.1m anchor depends on only four observations, restoring or revising those years could materially move the normalized OE in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every historical OE year from filed depreciation and amortization components—ordinary D&A, acquired-intangible amortization and other-asset amortization—counting each exactly once; restore valid years and rerun the log trend and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring acquisition spending could require an OE deduction or lower organic growth assumptions if acquired earnings support the anchor or forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: In fact, over the last three fiscal years we have completed seven acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing shows four FY2026 acquisitions with $282.7m of net acquisition cash outflow and seven acquisitions over three years. It also reports six percentage points of consolidated organic recurring-revenue growth versus 3%-6% valuation growth, so the record does not demonstrate that forecast growth requires acquisitions. Revenue growth, however, does not establish organic OE growth or whether the normalized earnings base includes acquisition-dependent benefits, leaving materiality unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an acquisition cohort schedule showing purchase cash, financing and integration costs, acquired revenue and OE by year, and organic OE growth; rerun growth or add a maintenance-acquisition allowance only if forecast OE requires recurring acquisitions.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge appears to add cash that may not be excess or distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $403.8m bridge maximum, equal to approximately $3.44 per share and 2.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-excess or restricted cash should be removed from the equity bridge rather than added to operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our subsidiaries through which we provide our business process outsourcing, fund processing, registered fund distribution, and transfer agency services are regulated and may be subject to restrictions on their ability to pay dividends to us.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates that the bridge approximates all $402.9m of reported cash, including $58.8m held by regulated entities and $241.0m held by foreign subsidiaries; it does not demonstrate how much is unavailable. Even eliminating the entire $403.8m bridge would reduce base value from $126.91 to about $123.47 per share and bull value from $148.49 to about $145.05, still below the $172.88 market price. Thus it cannot change the present valuation conclusion, although the bridge classification should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by entity and purpose, deduct minimum operating liquidity, regulated capital, customer-deposit support, accrued obligations and applicable repatriation taxes, and update the bridge and buy-below value.

audit_findings.title: Opaque stakes_net may omit claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Unnetted retirement, acquisition, software, tax or other liabilities would reduce stakes_net and the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain post-employment benefit obligations reported in our Consolidated Balance Sheets in the amount of $89.3 million as of June 30, 2026 were not included in the table above due to the uncertainty of the timing of these future payments.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies $89.3m of post-employment obligations, $70.8m of Rabbi Trust assets, $59.9m of contingent consideration, $128.4m of current and non-current software-license liabilities, and a $359.4m net deferred-tax liability. It does not show which assets or corresponding claims are already reflected in the opaque $411.1m stakes_net figure or recurring OE. An omission is therefore not demonstrated, and aggregating the filed balances would risk double counting, but the record cannot establish the remaining bridge exposure or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Produce a security-by-security and liability-by-liability stakes_net reconciliation, matching Rabbi Trust assets to benefits and testing contingent consideration, software liabilities, deferred taxes and other claims for inclusion elsewhere; rerun the bridge for verified omissions.

audit_findings.title: Temporary cash-tax benefits may have been capitalized as recurring OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $105.8m FY2026 deferred tax expense, $118.0m provision-to-cash-tax gap, and $359.4m year-end net deferred-tax liability; normalization effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Using temporarily reduced cash taxes can inflate FY2026 OE, the trend anchor and cash flows capitalized into perpetuity.
audit_findings.evidence: The changes result in a reduction to cash payments for income taxes but no material impact on the Company’s effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that FY2026 tax provision was $321.6m while cash taxes were $203.6m, deferred tax expense was $105.8m, and the legislation reduced cash payments without materially changing the effective tax rate. It does not establish whether the OE calculation used cash taxes or normalized provision taxes. The $105.8m deferred component equals 10.6% of the $1,001.1m anchor, making retained temporary benefits reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE tax charge to current and deferred tax expense, identify legislative and timing deferrals and their reversal schedule, normalize recurring taxes, and rerun the OE series, anchor and scenarios if cash-tax benefits were retained.
